policy.rule: A historical-context record whose ciphertext matches the review-trigger pattern is withheld from the canonical v0.7 dataset pending verification against a source. The pattern is not proof of fabrication.
policy.test: At least 20 A-Z letters with all letters distinct, or a contiguous run of the alphabet. None of the 100,272 synthetic records in v0.6 exhibits this pattern. Under the narrow baseline of independent, uniformly drawn A-Z letters, P(all 26 distinct) is about 6.6e-11 and P(all 25 distinct) about 1.7e-9. Those numbers are not the probability of fabrication, and other cipher or message models can yield distinct letters.
policy.why_not_regenerated: Re-encrypting the plaintext with a museum engine would produce a pair whose ciphertext came from a seeded pedagogical model rather than the machine named in the record. That is a synthetic exercise wearing a historical title, so the records are withdrawn from the canonical set rather than back-filled.
policy.preservation: Every excluded record remains in the immutable v0.6 archive and is listed with its evidence in public/corpus/v0.7/excluded-records.json. The IDs are retired, not reused.
